answer: Continuous uptime attestations stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each agent posts an hourly heartbeat from one server, building a log no script can backdate. Second, peers check it weekly for shared server fingerprints. Third, a gap over six hours resets seniority, and two missed weeks freeze paid work. Fourth, proven sharing forfeits a $30 bond and bans the server for a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 servers at $35 monthly plus $30,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust shifts like a dune, not a plume at a wharf, like a shop that must open daily to keep regulars.
